subject: Usage band, burst capacity, and hosted pricing — next steps
messages:
From: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@lynxcommerce.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + hosted pricing conversation follow-up

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call this morning — good walkthrough. Per our internal sizing exercise I wanted to capture the numbers we discussed and confirm a couple of assumptions before you send a formal hosted pricing quote. Rough baseline + peak profile below: 

- Expected steady-state (month 1-3): ~120M tokens / month (primarily chat sessions with short contexts ~300 tokens).
- Expected ramp (month 4-12): moving toward ~520–620M tokens / month as we expand to additional product flows.
- Typical peak TPS: sustained peaks around 40–60 TPS during traffic spikes.
- Burst scenario: intermittent spike to ~200 TPS for 2–6 minutes (holiday campaign + ML retraining window).
- Token mix: approx 70% input tokens, 30% generated tokens (avg generation 150 tokens).
- Target unit economics: we’re aiming for $/1M tokens in the neighborhood of $300–$360 to make this project ROI-positive.

Procurement timeline: procurement + legal will be ready to review a pricing/terms package in ~2 weeks. We prefer a hosted plan (no on-prem) but need clarity on burst headroom and whether any elevated SLA or burst credits are required.

Attachments: I’ve attached our internal forecast (for your sizing) and a short one-pager on traffic patterns. Please confirm whether the hosted pricing you’ll propose assumes prefix caching, and if we should plan for any separate burst reservations.

Cheers,
Tariq
VP Product, Lynx Commerce

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@lynxcommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + hosted pricing conversation follow-up

Hi Tariq — thanks for the clear summary. This is very helpful and aligns with what we saw on the call. A few clarifications from our side before we draft the formal quote:

1) Commit vs PAYG: Do you expect to sign up to a committed monthly token slab for a 12-month term, or do you want a pay-as-you-go hosted plan with burst add-ons? Commit gives materially lower $/1M token pricing; PAYG is simpler but higher on unit cost.

2) Burst tolerance: For hosted, we can handle short bursts automatically up to a platform limit. For repeated sustained bursts (200 TPS for >10 minutes), we recommend either a temporary burst reservation or a short-duration Dedicated pool. From your note, intermittent 2–6 minute bursts look fine on hosted without a reservation, but we’ll dimension the headroom in the quote.

3) Observability and cost control: We’ll include an estimate showing expected cost under three scenarios (baseline, ramp to 600M, and burst-heavy). That will include token-level breakdown and a target $/1M token for each slab. If the $300–$360 target is the goal, we’ll flag the commit size required to reach that band.

I’ve attached a preliminary pricing worksheet with three tiered bands and asked Rishi to add a short note on caching and request routing that will materially change the effective $/1M.

Next steps: I’ll turn this into a formal quote + MOU draft by Monday (2028-06-18) so you can share with procurement. Can you confirm which commitment horizon you’d prefer (monthly flexible / 6 months / 12 months)?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@lynxcommerce.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + hosted pricing conversation follow-up

Tariq — quick technical addendum from the solutions side.

- Caching impact: With prefix/KV caching we often see 15–25% effective token reduction for chat-heavy flows if prompts are highly templated. If you can confirm reuse of system prompts or shared context across users, we’ll bake a conservative 12% token-reduction assumption into the estimate.
- Concurrency vs TPS: TPS is a good high-level metric; we’ll also model concurrency and average response latency. For short-lived bursts (2–6 minutes), the platform’s autoscaler will spin up additional capacity; the only cost implication is a short window of higher GPU usage.
- Burst protection: For your 200 TPS spikes, we recommend the hosted option with burst credits enabled (no immediate need for Dedicated). Burst credits are charged as a flat per-minute premium during the elevated window — I’ll include sample math so you can see true $/1M converted for those minutes.
- Security/compliance: hosted will meet Lynx’s requirements assuming standard SOC2 + encrypted-at-rest. If procurement needs customer-managed KMS we can add that as an enterprise option.

I’ve uploaded a short calc to the quote link (see related_links) and left notes in the attached pricing worksheet.

—Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@lynxcommerce.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + hosted pricing conversation follow-up

Thanks all — that level of detail is perfect. Confirming the procurement direction:

- Preference: 12-month commitment if the headline $/1M tokens can be mid-band ($~350).
- We’re ok with hosted provided you include burst credits in the package and show the incremental cost for a single 6-minute 200 TPS event.
- Please include a line item for a one-time security review + SOC2 evidence package (procurement will likely ask).

Next steps for us: I’ll share your MOU/quote with procurement on Monday and aim to get feedback within 7–10 business days. Please send the formal quote + draft MOU and the updated pricing worksheet to tariq@lynxcommerce.com and procurement@lynxcommerce.com.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Tariq
VP Product, Lynx Commerce
